require-async-module.title: Runbook: use dynamic import() instead of require(), from an async caller (a top-level module, or inside an async function)
Runbook: if the requiring file itself can become an ES module, convert it (rename to .mjs, or add "type": "module") and use a real import declaration

dirname-undefined-in-esm.title: Runbook: use import.meta.dirname (Node 20.11+/21.2+; this corpus verified it live on 24.7.0 and 24.8.0)
Runbook: on an older supported Node, derive it instead: path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))

require-undefined-in-esm.title: Runbook: use a real import declaration (or dynamic import()) instead of require
Runbook: if a CJS-only dependency genuinely has no ESM-compatible way to load it, build a real require function for this one module: const require = createRequire(import.meta.url), from node:module

top-level-await-in-cjs.title: Runbook: wrap the awaiting code in an async IIFE, (async () => { ... })(), and let that promise's rejection be handled explicitly rather than awaited at the top level
Runbook: if the file can become an ES module (rename to .mjs, or add "type": "module"), top-level await works there directly with no wrapper
